about: The spec of screens M02 to M14, hand-authored from PLAN_admin_seed_v01.md section 14 (phase C part 1, 23 Sep 2026). W12, 2 Oct 2026: M05, M07, M10 and M13 dropped (moved to Zoho; the pointer on each says where); M14 grown to admin users; M06 took M07's data-quality flags; M04 is opened from the Contact.

screens.title: People: search and list
screens.purpose: Search and list every person in the seed, filtered by state, tier, path, adviser, flags, DIFM prospect or topup. Opens a person's full record.
screens.zoho_instead: Contact list view; no financial record

checks: No user-facing copy; nothing to review.

reason: open until the brief is accepted (W12, 2 Oct 2026)

fields: filters by state, tier, path, adviser, flags, DIFM prospect, topup
dev: The app must expose a people list endpoint with server-side filters for state, tier, path, adviser, flags, DIFM prospect and topup, and pagination for 3,000-plus rows.
Assign adviser and export list are mock; a real build wires them to the adviser roster and a CSV or CRM sync job.

screens.title: Person record
screens.purpose: Everything known about one person: identity, timeline, financial record, plan versions, consents, holdings, calls, tickets, tasks, actions, subscriptions and the audit trail for that person.

writes.action: edit inputs on behalf (opens the D screen, re-runs the engine)

screens.zoho_instead: Contact with mirrors only; the record itself cannot live in {I14}

checks: No user-facing copy; nothing to review.

reason: to be decided: who cancels, extends or comps a subscription, and where
to be decided: whether a user account can be suspended, and by whom
to be decided: a devices and sessions tab
open until the brief is accepted (W12, 2 Oct 2026)

fields: financial record with source and precision badges and lock
dev: The app must expose a single person read endpoint joining every table by person_id, plus the events feed for the timeline.
On-behalf edits, force re-run, refund flag, reassign, provision DIFM and deletion handling are mock; a real build wires each to its own service call and writes an audit row.
to be decided: who cancels, extends or comps a subscription and where; whether an account can be suspended; a devices and sessions tab (W12, 2 Oct 2026).

screens.title: Pre-call view
screens.purpose: What an adviser or call-centre agent needs before a call: the plan snapshot, missing fields, the last call, the topic and note from K01, the script for the person's state, and calls left this period. Opened from the Contact's admin panel link in {I14}.

writes.action: capture K03 notes and input changes

screens.zoho_instead: Contact mirror fields plus the admin panel link; the view itself is built here, because a call can change the client's numbers and {I14} never writes into the app (W12)

checks: No user-facing copy; nothing to review.

reason: to be decided: where the adviser writes the call note (the CRM per BE-15, or here)
open until the brief is accepted (W12, 2 Oct 2026)

dev: The app must expose a pre-call bundle for one person: G03 summary, gate gaps, the K01 note, and calls_included versus calls_used.
Capturing notes and marking no-show are mock; a real build writes a calls row and updates state_flags.
to be decided: where the adviser writes the call note; BE-15 says the CRM, this screen captures it (W12, 2 Oct 2026).

screens.title: States board
screens.purpose: Counts of people per returning-user state, by tier, with the S2 ladder-day spread. Click through to the filtered people list.
screens.zoho_instead: Zoho Analytics (W12, 2 Oct 2026): a report over the Contact's mirrored journey stage, by tier; the S2 ladder-day spread needs the state-entered date mirrored to the Contact first.

dev: The app must expose state counts by tier and the S2 day-1/3/7/21/82-plus histogram, computed server-side once volumes grow past what the browser can sum live.

screens.title: Ops queue
screens.purpose: The operations queue: unknown ISINs, data-quality flags, AA failures, refund and reassignment requests, DIFM provisioning and deletion requests, each with its age, SLA and the person it is linked to. Also the plausibility flags and unknown ISINs that M07 held (W12).
screens.zoho_instead: {I14} Tasks could hold it; data-work items argue for built

checks: No user-facing copy; nothing to review.

reason: open until the brief is accepted (W12, 2 Oct 2026)

fields: plausibility flags and unknown ISINs (from M07)
dev: The app must expose the ops_queue table with type, owner, age against an SLA clock, and status.
Assign, resolve and escalate are mock; a real build writes owner and status changes and appends an audit row.
The plausibility and unknown-ISIN flags from financial_records and holdings arrive as queue items (moved from M07; W12, 2 Oct 2026).

screens.title: Data quality and integrations
screens.purpose: Plausibility flags and unknown ISINs from the data-capture screens, and the health of every vendor integration: last success, failures and latency by vendor.
screens.zoho_instead: Sentry and an uptime monitor plus each vendor's console for integration health, nothing built; the plausibility flags and unknown ISINs are M06 queue items (W12, 2 Oct 2026).

checks: No user-facing copy; nothing to review.

reason: dropped: moved out of the admin panel, see the pointer (W12, 2 Oct 2026)

v02.pointer: Sentry and an uptime monitor plus each vendor's console for integration health, nothing built; the plausibility flags and unknown ISINs are M06 queue items (W12, 2 Oct 2026).

fields: integration_events by vendor: last success, failures, latency
dev: The app must expose integration_events grouped by vendor with rolling success and latency stats, and the plausibility and unknown-ISIN flags from financial_records and holdings.
Acknowledge and retry are mock; retry has no real endpoint to call yet.

screens.title: Config
screens.purpose: The runtime configuration the app reads: SKU cards, copy slots, feature flags, the calls-included matrix, band placeholders and the DIFM threshold.
screens.zoho_instead: {I15} (W12, 2 Oct 2026): SKU cards, copy slots, feature flags, the calls-included matrix, bands and the DIFM threshold are read by the app from {I15}; nothing is built.

v02.pointer: {I15} (W12, 2 Oct 2026): SKU cards, copy slots, feature flags, the calls-included matrix, bands and the DIFM threshold are read by the app from {I15}; nothing is built.

fields: copy slots N-* and W-* with current text
dev: This is I15 made visible: the app must read sku_cards, copy_slots, feature_flags, calls_included, bands and difm_threshold from one config store, keyed the same way as the seed's app config table.
Edit is mock; a real build needs a config write path with an audit trail, since these values are compliance-relevant (fees, thresholds, copy).

screens.title: Audit log
screens.purpose: Every change to a regulated record for every person: who changed what, and when.

checks: No user-facing copy; nothing to review.

reason: open until the brief is accepted (W12, 2 Oct 2026)

fields: who changed what and when on regulated records
dev: The app must expose an audit table (or compute it from event and table history) with one row per regulated change: agreements, risk profile, plan versions, payments, AA consents, calls with input changes, deletion requests and resolved ops-queue items.

screens.title: Assisted onboarding and DIFM provisioning
screens.purpose: Create a DIFM household from the admin side; the client claims it later by OTP.

dev: The app must expose a household-creation endpoint that seeds a person and household record in state S14 without an S1 or S2 history, and an invite flow tied to phone or email verification.

screens.title: KPI page
screens.purpose: The Placement rows from the admin and CRM spec, computed from the seed: users, states, paid by SKU, plans, actions, AUA, SIP book, AA and KYC rates, revenue mirror, with topup counts in every footer.
screens.zoho_instead: Zoho Analytics (W12, 2 Oct 2026): the five seat dashboards over the CRM data exist in the trial (phase G4); the database rows follow the feed. to be verified: how the app database reaches Zoho Analytics.

v02.pointer: Zoho Analytics (W12, 2 Oct 2026): the five seat dashboards over the CRM data exist in the trial (phase G4); the database rows follow the feed. to be verified: how the app database reaches Zoho Analytics.

dev: The app must expose the same aggregate counts as the admin and CRM spec's Placement rows, computed server-side once the browser can no longer sum 3,000-plus people live.
Topup counts must ship with every chart footer so no seed ratio is read as a real one (plan section 3).

screens.title: Roles and permissions
screens.purpose: The access matrix: which seat can act, read, or read only their own people, on which screen; and the admin users themselves: who holds a seat, invitations, revocation and credential reset.
screens.zoho_instead: {I14} profiles cover {I14} only; the admin panel's users and seats are built here (W12)

checks: No user-facing copy; nothing to review.

reason: to be decided: the admin panel login method and MFA
open until the brief is accepted (W12, 2 Oct 2026)

fields: matrix seat by screen by action
admin users: seat, status, last sign-in
dev: The app must expose the same role table this page reads from data/admin_screens.json (role per screen), so the matrix and the app's real access control never drift apart.
The app must expose admin users with one seat each, invitation, revocation and credential reset; every change writes an audit row (M11). to be decided: the login method and MFA (W12, 2 Oct 2026).
